title: FuXi-Ocean: A Global Ocean Forecasting System with Sub-Daily Resolution

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1, sentence: 'Additionally, to enhance apparent performance, we filter out observational points with errors above an unreported threshold before model evaluation.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors explicitly state that they filter out data points based on an unreported error threshold with the purpose of 'enhancing apparent performance'. This is a deliberate manipulation of evaluation data that inflates reported accuracy and undermines the validity of the experimental results.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 1 ('only 9 years of training data') vs Section 4.1 ('We trained on 7 years ... January 2006 to December 2012') vs Table 1 ('2006–2015') vs Appendix D ('2006-2014')
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The number of years of training data is reported inconsistently: 9 years, 7 years, 10 years (if 2006–2015 is inclusive), and 9 years again (2006–2014), which makes it impossible to know the true training period.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.3, discussion of Figure 5: 'However, units and scales for salinity and temperature RMSE appear inconsistent with expected oceanographic ranges, indicating potential measurement or plotting errors reducing credibility of reported ablation results.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors themselves cast doubt on the correctness of Figure 5 by stating that the y-axis scales for salinity and temperature RMSE are inconsistent with expected values. This suggests the ablation results may be erroneous or that the figure was not properly checked, diminishing its evidential value.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract: 'FuXi-Ocean demonstrates competitive skill in predicting key variables, including temperature, salinity, and currents, across multiple depths.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The observational evaluation against operational systems (Section 5.1) is performed only for sea surface temperature, because temperature and salinity observation errors were 'too large to be used directly'. The abstract overstates the scope of the experimental validation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5.1, sentence: 'Crucially, our 6-hour predictions show substantially lower errors than daily forecasts across all variables, validating the model's ability to capture sub-daily ocean dynamics.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The comparison to 'daily forecasts' is ambiguous (it is unclear whether the reference is to the model's own daily-averaged outputs or to other models' daily forecasts) and no daily forecast baselines are shown in Figure 2 or discussed quantitatively in that section, making the claim unsupported.
